note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

nodes.name: WER is lexical only
nodes.description: WER treats all lexical errors equally and measures only verbatim recall, ignoring how transcription errors propagate to semantic understanding and task completion; two transcripts with identical WER (29%) can differ drastically in meaning.

nodes.name: End-to-end models lack transcripts
nodes.description: End-to-end voice LLMs bypass explicit ASR transcription, so WER-based evaluation does not apply and there is no unified metric comparing cascaded and end-to-end systems.

nodes.name: Bloom-based three-level test
nodes.description: SpeechIQ evaluates LLM-Voice at three levels from Bloom's Taxonomy: Remember (WER), Understand (hidden-state similarity of LLM responses), and Apply (multiple-choice QA accuracy).

nodes.name: Understand-level similarity metric
nodes.description: The Understand score prompts an LLM (LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct) to give a one-word background and one-word summary of the speech, and takes the lower of the cosine similarities between last-layer hidden states for ASR transcript and ground-truth transcript.

nodes.name: Apply-level QA construction
nodes.description: For each speech sample, 3 questions with 5 choices (including 'None of the above') are generated by GPT-4o from the ground-truth transcript, filtered so GPT-4o and Gemini-1.5-flash answer them correctly, and answered 5 times with majority vote.

nodes.name: SIQ aggregation
nodes.description: SIQ combines the three levels via per-sample discrimination weights (inter-model variance), global standardization, and inverse-variance dimension weights, converted to an IQ-like scale SIQ = 100 + 15 * Score.

nodes.name: Remember-level results
nodes.description: On WER, Canary is best, GER (Whisper-v2 5-best + GPT-4o) increases WER relative to plain ASR, and all cascaded ASR models outperform all end-to-end models including Gemini-1.5.

nodes.name: Apply-level results
nodes.description: Similar-size end-to-end models have much lower QA accuracy than cascaded ones, scaled-up end-to-end models (Gemini-1.5, Baichuan-omni) do best, and GER improves downstream reasoning.

nodes.name: WER ranking does not predict SIQ
nodes.description: Single ASR models lead on WER but lose their lead on higher-level intelligence; GER gives stable SIQ improvements and ASR+GER+LLM reaches the best SIQ (e.g. 108.64 for Whisperv2+GPT-4o+Qwen2-7B).

nodes.name: SIQ matches human preference best
nodes.description: On human rankings of 10 models over 9 examples, SIQ_all has Spearman rho 0.952 (p=0.00002), higher than WER (0.770), SemDist (0.721), LLM-S (0.624), BLEU (0.806) and SIQ_rm (0.830).

nodes.name: Cascaded beats end-to-end at same base model
nodes.description: With the same foundation LLM, cascaded variants outperform end-to-end models on all three levels, notably Qwen2-Audio and Salmonn at the Apply level (e.g. Salmonn accuracy 60.3 vs 87.3 for Whisper+Vicuna), suggesting multi-modal training may sacrifice reasoning ability.

nodes.name: Annotation errors via unanswerable QA
nodes.description: QA that most LLM-Voice models fail identifies annotation errors: only 26 of 800 samples needed human review, and 17 were confirmed truly unanswerable, forming an unanswerable set.

nodes.name: Hallucination detection
nodes.description: On the unanswerable set, answering anything other than 'None of the above' counts as hallucination; LLaMA3-8B-Instruct hallucinates much more (41.2% cascaded, 70.6% in its end-to-end variant Desta2), explaining Desta2's unexpectedly high apply accuracy.

nodes.name: Hallucination inheritance
nodes.description: Hallucination of a foundation LLM is inherited by its multimodal variants, making foundation model selection and hallucination reduction important in multimodal training.

nodes.name: Higher intelligence helps end-to-end apply
nodes.description: Using Gemini-1.5-flash as ASR with a cascaded LLM lowers apply accuracy (96.6 end-to-end vs 95.1 cascaded) while the small Qwen2-Audio gains slightly (83.9 to 84.2); humans reach 99.27 apply accuracy despite 53.67 WER, suggesting higher intelligence benefits higher-order levels even with imperfect transcription.

isolated_nodes.name: Datasets and architectures
isolated_nodes.description: Evaluation uses subsets of Earnings22, VoxPopuli and Med-ASR-EN (the longest audios) across ASR+LLM, ASR+GER+LLM and end-to-end architectures.

isolated_nodes.name: Limitation: moderate test sets
isolated_nodes.description: Evaluation is based on moderately sized test sets, and the study focuses on voice understanding with text outputs only.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from WER's limitations to a three-level cognitive evaluation, its scoring, empirical comparison of architectures, and by-products (annotation errors, hallucination detection).
